mainTopic: Whether אונס counts in a conditional גט, how רבנן can cancel קידושין, and when the Wednesday wedding rule applies
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining רבא's first version, that אונס does not cancel a conditional גט. One explanation is the worry about צנועות, who could wrongly stay stuck. The other is the worry about פרוצות, who could wrongly remarry. The גמרא asks how רבנן can free a woman whom the תורה would keep married. It answers that every man marries on the terms of רבנן, so they can cancel the קידושין, and if the קידושין were made through ביאה, they make it בעילת זנות. A second version of רבא says the opposite: אונס does count in גיטין. The גמרא tests this version against a משנה about 'if I don't return within twelve months' and against שמואל's case of the man stopped by the ferry. Each challenge is answered: death is a special case, and a common אונס is the husband's own fault for not planning. Finally, רב שמואל בר יצחק explains that the Wednesday wedding rule depends on courts sitting on Monday and Thursday. Where courts sit every day and the groom has already prepared the feast, a woman may marry on any day.

steps.title: The concern for virtuous women: she may wrongly stay an עגונה
steps.stepSummary: If the גט did not take effect when the husband was held back by אונס, a modest woman might wrongly think he was held back and never remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes he was not really held back, but she thinks he was, so she stays stuck as an עגונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of the first reason, צנועות (virtuous women), for saying that אונס does not cancel a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words just before this said: 'if you say it would not be a גט when he was held back by אונס.' Under that rule, a careful woman who cannot know what really happened might assume he was held back. She would then treat herself as still married, even though she is actually divorced, and never remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: Held back by forces beyond his control (אונס)
She becomes an עגונה, a woman stuck and unable to remarry

phrases.english: Sometimes he was not held back by forces beyond his control
phrases.notes: The start of this sentence, 'if you say it would not be a גט,' came just before this.

phrases.english: but she thinks that he was held back,
so she stays stuck and sits as an עגונה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the צנועות reason, which began before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If אונס cancelled the גט, a modest woman might wrongly think he was held back and stay an עגונה when she is really free.

steps.title: The concern for licentious women: her children could become ממזרים
steps.stepSummary: If אונס cancelled the גט, a careless woman might assume he was not held back and remarry while still married, so her children would be ממזרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And because of careless women: if you say it is not a גט, then sometimes he really was held back, but she says he wasn't. She goes and remarries, the גט turns out to be void, and her children are ממזרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second reason, פרוצות (careless women), for saying that אונס does not cancel a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite risk from the first reason. Here the woman is too quick to assume she is free. If the גט were really cancelled because of אונס, she would be a married woman marrying someone else, and her children would be ממזרים. On the previous amud these two reasons are given as two different versions ('some say... and some say...'), not as two reasons said together.

keyTerms.meaning: A void גט that does not work
Children born from a forbidden union, such as with a married woman

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רבא holds that the גט works even in a case of אונס. One explanation is the worry about צנועות, who could wrongly stay stuck. The other explanation is the worry about פרוצות, who could wrongly remarry.

phrases.english: And because of careless women —
for if you say it should not be a גט,
sometimes he was held back by forces beyond his control
and she says he was not held back,
and she goes and marries someone else,
and it turns out the גט is void
and her children are ממזרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the two reasons, right after the צנועות reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If אונס cancelled the גט, a careless woman might remarry while still married, and her children would be ממזרים.

steps.title: How can רבנן permit a married woman to others?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבנן can make a גט work when, by תורה law, it would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really a case where by תורה law it is not a גט, and yet, because of modest women and careless women, we let a married woman marry anyone?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule it just explained. It asks how רבנן could have the power to do this at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law, a man held back by אונס is not held responsible, so the condition should not count and the גט should not take effect. That means she is still a married woman. How can a rabbinic reason, however good, let an אשת איש marry another man, which is a serious תורה prohibition?

keyTerms.meaning: To everyone, so she may marry anyone

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבנן are wrong. It is asking where their power to change her status comes from.

phrases.english: And is there really such a thing
where by תורה law it is not a גט,
and because of modest women and because of careless women
we permit a married woman to the whole world?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא לֶהֱוֵי גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule that steps 1 and 2 just explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a גט works even when the husband was held back by אונס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By תורה law she is still married, so a rabbinic concern should not be able to let an אשת איש remarry.

steps.title: Every marriage depends on רבנן, so they can cancel it
steps.stepSummary: Yes, they can. Everyone marries on the terms of רבנן, so רבנן can cancel the קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. Anyone who marries a woman does so on the terms set by רבנן, and רבנן took his קידושין away from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining where the power of רבנן comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן are not permitting an אשת איש. Since every man marries on the condition that רבנן agree, when רבנן cancel the קידושין, the marriage is undone. Once that happens, she was never really married to him, so she may marry someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: On the terms set by רבנן
Marriage, the first stage of marriage

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that רבנן can cancel קידושין because every marriage depends on their terms, is used in several places in the גמרא.

phrases.english: Yes, anyone who marries a woman
marries her on the terms set by רבנן,
and רבנן took his קידושין away from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, כׇּל דִּמְקַדֵּשׁ אַדַּעְתָּא דְּרַבָּנַן מְקַדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the source of the power: the marriage itself depends on רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבנן seem to be letting an אשת איש remarry against תורה law.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן cancel the קידושין, so she is no longer an אשת איש at all.

steps.title: רבינא asks: what about קידושין done through ביאה?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי how cancelling works when the קידושין were done through ביאה rather than money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: That works if he married her with money. But if he married her through ביאה, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the answer of step 4 by pointing to a kind of קידושין where cancelling seems hard to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With money, רבנן can treat the money as if it never belonged to him, so the קידושין never happened. But a physical act of ביאה actually took place. How can רבנן undo something that really happened?

keyTerms.meaning: Marital relations, one of the ways to make קידושין

phrases.english: רבינא said to רב אשי:
That works if he married her with money.
phrases.notes: The money can be treated as if it was never his, so the קידושין never took effect.

phrases.english: If he married her through ביאה,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי תִּינַח קַדֵּישׁ בְּכַסְפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the answer of step 4 can reach.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבנן can cancel any קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money can be treated as if it never belonged to him, but a physical act of ביאה cannot simply be erased.

steps.title: רבנן made the ביאה into בעילת זנות
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבנן gave his act the status of an act outside of marriage, so it does not make קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן made his act of ביאה into בעילת זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered (this is understood as רב אשי replying). Even קידושין through ביאה can be undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן do not deny that the act happened. They change what it means legally: it counts as בעילת זנות, an act outside of marriage, not an act of קידושין. So there were never any קידושין, and the woman is free.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it into, they gave it the status of
An act of relations outside of marriage, with no קידושין

steps.whatToRemember: The power of רבנן to cancel קידושין works both ways: with money they treat the money as not his, and with ביאה they treat the act as בעילת זנות.

phrases.english: רבנן made it into
his act of relations an act outside of marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the legal status of the act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An act of ביאה that really happened cannot be undone.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן made it count as בעילת זנות, so it never made קידושין.

steps.title: Another version: רבא says אונס does count for a גט
steps.stepSummary: According to a second version, רבא said that the rule of אונס applies to גיטין too. So in his view, a man who was held back by circumstances out of his control is not treated as having broken the condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבא said, 'And the same is true for divorce documents.' So it seems that רבא holds that אונס counts when it comes to a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, opposite version of what רבא said. In this version, the idea that אונס counts also applies to גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבא said אונס does NOT count for a גט, because of the worry about צנועות or פרוצות (Steps 1-2). This version flips that. If a man made his גט depend on a condition and was held back by circumstances out of his control, the condition is not treated as broken, so the גט does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Being forced by circumstances out of one's control
'So it seems', which draws a conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion of a different person. It is another version of the same statement of רבא, and it says the opposite of the first version.

phrases.english: Some say: Rava said,
and the same is true regarding bills of divorce.
phrases.notes: 'The same' means the rule just taught about a wedding delayed by אונס, where אונס counts.

phrases.english: Apparently Rava holds:
Circumstances beyond one's control count for bills of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא דאמרי: אמר רבא, וכן לענין גיטין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבא's statement that is the opposite of the version discussed in Steps 1 to 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רבא holds that אונס counts for a גט, so a condition broken through אונס is not treated as broken.

steps.title: A challenge from the משנה about 'if I don't come back in twelve months'
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if the husband dies within the twelve months, the גט does not work. This implies that if he only fell sick, it would work, so sickness (אונס) does not save him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: 'Here is your גט if I don't come back from now until twelve months,' and he died within the twelve months. It is not a גט. Only when he died is it not a גט. But if he got sick, it is a גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version of רבא using a משנה about a conditional גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says that death cancels the גט. That suggests other kinds of אונס, like sickness, do not cancel it, and the גט takes effect. That would mean אונס does not count for גיטין, which goes against this version of רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is your גט', the wording used when giving a גט

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'This is your bill of divorce
if I do not come back
from now until twelve months,'
and he died within the twelve months:
it is not a bill of divorce.
It is when he died that it is not a divorce;
but if he fell sick, it is a divorce!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 7's claim that אונס counts for גיטין.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view (second version) that אונס counts for a גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By mentioning only death, the משנה implies that sickness, which is also אונס, would not stop the גט from taking effect. So אונס does not count.

steps.title: Sickness also cancels it; death was mentioned to teach no גט after death
steps.stepSummary: The answer: if he fell sick, it is also not a גט. The משנה chose the case of death to teach that a גט cannot take effect after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you that if he got sick, it is also not a גט. And the משנה is teaching us this point itself: there is no גט after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the inference from the משנה and explains why the משנה picked the case of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death was not mentioned because it is the only kind of אונס that cancels the גט. Sickness would cancel it too. The משנה used death because it wanted to teach a separate rule: a גט cannot take effect once the husband is dead.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really, I can tell you', which introduces an answer that keeps the original position
'It teaches us', meaning the new point being taught
A גט cannot take effect after the husband's death

phrases.english: Actually, I will tell you
if he fell sick it is also not a divorce,
and this itself is what it teaches us:
that there is no divorce after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: לעולם אימא לך חלה נמי אינו גט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the inference: the case was chosen for a different teaching purpose.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning only death implies sickness would not cancel the גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sickness also cancels the גט. Death is mentioned to teach that there is no גט after death.

steps.title: But 'no גט after death' was already taught earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why would the משנה need to teach that there is no גט after death? An earlier clause already taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There is no גט after death'? But the earlier part of the משנה already taught that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 9. The rule it gave is already known from an earlier clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה does not repeat itself for no reason. If 'no גט after death' was already taught in the רישא, it cannot be the reason the משנה mentioned death here. So the inference about sickness seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: The earlier or first clause of a משנה

phrases.english: 'There is no divorce after death'?
But he already taught it in the first clause!

steps.triggerLanguage: אין גט לאחר מיתה הא תנא ליה רישא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה mentioned death in order to teach 'no גט after death'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule already appears in the רישא, so repeating it here would be pointless. So the case of death must be there to exclude sickness.

steps.title: The repetition comes to reject the view of רבותינו
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה may repeat the case of death in order to rule against רבותינו, who held otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it comes to exclude the view of רבותינו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה repeats the case of death even though an earlier clause covered it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition is not wasted. It comes to reject the view of רבותינו, who held differently in this kind of case. So the case of death has its own purpose, and nothing can be learned from it about sickness. רבא's second version still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To exclude', meaning to reject another view
'Our Rabbis', a specific group of חכמים whose view is quoted elsewhere

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, רבא holds that אונס counts for a גט. The משנה about 'if I don't come back in twelve months' does not prove otherwise. Death is mentioned to teach that there is no גט after death, and to reject the view of רבותינו. Sickness would also cancel the גט.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is to exclude the view of our Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10, so the answer of Step 9 still holds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a purpose for the repetition: it rejects another opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating the rule that there is no גט after death would be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The repetition rejects the view of רבותינו. So the case of death says nothing about sickness, and רבא's second version stands.

steps.title: The later clause of the משנה: he said 'from now' and then died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the same משנה. If the husband said 'from now' and died within twelve months, the גט works. It infers that the same would be true if he only fell sick, so אונס would not help him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'From now, if I have not come back within twelve months,' and he died within the twelve months, it is a גט. Doesn't this mean the same is true if he fell sick?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source to attack רבא's second version, which says אונס applies to גיטין. It uses the later clause of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he said 'from now', the גט can take effect while he is still alive, so his death does not block it. The גמרא then suggests that sickness should be no different. If so, being held back by circumstances out of his control does not stop the condition, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: From now: the גט takes effect from the moment it is given, if the condition is later met

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"From now, if I have not come back
from now until twelve months,"
and he died within the twelve months,
this is a valid bill of divorce.
Is it not that the same is true if he fell sick!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer about רבותינו in step 11, the גמרא turns to the next clause of the same משנה for a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's second version: אונס applies to גיטין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the גט works when he died (an אונס), then it should also work when he fell sick, so אונס does not cancel the condition.

steps.title: Death is special because he wants to spare her from the יבם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. Only in the case of death does the husband want the גט to work, so that his wife will not need יבום. In sickness he would not want it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, only in the case of death, because he does not want her to fall before the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the משנה's ruling is limited to death and cannot be stretched to sickness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband who gives a גט 'from now' is happy for it to work if he dies, because then his wife is divorced and does not need יבום or חליצה from his brother. That reason does not exist if he only fell sick. So in sickness he would not want the גט to work, and רבא's rule of אונס still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not comfortable with it, he does not want it
The husband's brother, who would do יבום if the husband dies without children

phrases.english: No, only when he died,
because he does not want
that she should fall before the yavam.
phrases.notes: Literally 'fall before': if he dies without children, she would be tied to his brother for יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by limiting the משנה to death.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (דוקא): the ruling is tied to a reason that applies only to death.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Death and sickness are both אונס, so they should be treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Death is unique because the husband wants his wife freed from the יבם, so the case proves nothing about sickness.

steps.title: The man stopped by the ferry: שמואל says it is not called coming
steps.stepSummary: A man made his גט depend on returning within thirty days. He arrived on time but the ferry kept him on the other side of the river. שמואל ruled this is not considered coming, which seems to show that אונס does not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from a man who said, 'If I do not come within thirty days, let it be a גט.' He came at the end of thirty days, but the ferry held him back. He shouted, 'See that I came! See that I came!' and שמואל said that is not called coming.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case ruled by שמואל as another challenge to רבא's second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man truly tried to return, and only the ferry being on the other side stopped him, which is a clear אונס. Yet שמואל said the condition was broken and the גט works. This seems to prove that אונס does not save a husband in גיטין.

keyTerms.meaning: A ferry, a boat for crossing the river

phrases.english: Come and hear from a certain man who said to them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the people he sent with the גט.

phrases.aramaic: ״אִי לָא אָתֵינָא מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
phrases.english: "If I do not come from now until thirty days,
let it be a bill of divorce."
He came at the end of thirty days,
and the ferry cut him off,
and he said to them: "See that I came! See that I came!"
And Shmuel said: That is not called coming!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a new challenge from a ruling of שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's second version: אונס applies to גיטין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The man was held back by an אונס (the ferry), yet שמואל treated the condition as broken, so אונס does not help in גיטין.

steps.title: A common אונס is different: he should have planned for it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a common, predictable אונס is different. The husband should have included it in his condition, and since he did not, he brought the loss on himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אונס that is common is different. Since he should have made a condition about it and did not, he caused the loss to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside the proof from שמואל by splitting אונס into two kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ferry being on the other side of the river happens all the time, so the husband could have expected it. Because he did not include it in his condition, he cannot claim אונס. רבא's rule still holds for a rare, unexpected אונס.

keyTerms.meaning: A common, predictable circumstance out of one's control
To make a condition, to state an exception
He caused the loss to himself

steps.whatToRemember: These sources do not disprove רבא's second version. Death is special because of the יבם, and a common אונס is different because he should have planned for it.

phrases.english: An unavoidable circumstance that is common is different,
because since he should have made a condition about it
and he did not make that condition,
he is the one who caused the loss to himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by separating a common אונס from a rare one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the category: common אונס versus rare אונס.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every אונס should be treated the same, so שמואל's ruling shows that אונס never helps.
steps.terutzMaskana: A common, predictable אונס is the husband's own fault for not planning; a rare אונס can still excuse him.

steps.title: The Wednesday wedding rule began with תקנת עזרא
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק says the rule that a בתולה marries on Wednesday applies only since תקנת עזרא, which set the courts to sit only on Monday and Thursday. Before that, courts sat every day, and a woman could marry on any day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: They taught this only from תקנת עזרא and on, when courts sit only on Monday and Thursday. But before תקנת עזרא, when courts sat every day, a woman could marry on any day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of אונס and goes back to our משנה, which says a בתולה marries on Wednesday. רב שמואל בר יצחק explains when that rule started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for Wednesday is that a husband with a complaint about virginity can go to court the next morning, Thursday. That only works once the courts sit on fixed days, Monday and Thursday. When courts sat every day, any day of the week was fine for a wedding.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this rule in this case

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the Wednesday rule depends on the court schedule, so the reason behind the rule decides when it applies.

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מִתַּקָּנַת עֶזְרָא וְאֵילָךְ,
phrases.english: They taught this only from the enactment of Ezra and onward,
phrases.notes: 'This' is our משנה's rule that a בתולה marries on Wednesday.

phrases.english: when courts are not in regular session
except on Monday and Thursday.
But before the enactment of Ezra,
when courts were in regular session every day,
a woman could be married on any day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of אונס and returns to explain the time frame of the משנה's Wednesday rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that a בתולה marries on Wednesday applies only since תקנת עזרא set the courts to sit on Monday and Thursday. Before that, a woman could marry on any day.

steps.title: Why talk about the past?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שמואל בר יצחק: what happened before תקנת עזרא is over, so why state it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Before the תקנה of עזרא? What was, was! Why does it matter now?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the statement from Step 16. Telling us how things worked before עזרא seems to have no practical use today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a teaching should give a working הלכה. Describing old history does not seem to teach anything we can act on. So it asks what the point of the statement is.

keyTerms.meaning: What was, was. The past is over and makes no practical difference

phrases.english: Before the ordinance of Ezra?
What was, was!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical relevance of the מימרא in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמואל בר יצחק's statement that before תקנת עזרא a woman could marry any day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A historical fact with no present-day result is not worth teaching

steps.title: The statement gives a rule for today
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק means: if courts today sit every day, as they did before עזרא, a woman may marry on any day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: if there are courts that sit regularly today, as before the תקנה of עזרא, a woman may marry on any day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the statement is not just history. It teaches a practical rule for any place where the courts sit every day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for Wednesday was so the husband could go to court on Thursday with a claim about virginity. If a court is available every day, that reason does not apply. So the old situation becomes a model for places today.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the Wednesday rule depends on its reason. Where the reason is missing, the rule can change.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
If there are courts
that sit regularly nowadays
phrases.notes: Regularly here means every day, not only on Monday and Thursday.

phrases.english: as before the ordinance of Ezra —
a woman is married on any day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the statement as practical
steps.terutzMaskana: Wherever courts sit daily today, a woman may marry on any day

steps.title: The feast-preparation reason still applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: we also need the reason of שקדו, that the groom has days to prepare the feast, which still points to Wednesday.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we also need the reason of 'they were careful' (that the groom should prepare the feast for several days)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 18. Even with courts every day, there is a second reason for Wednesday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wednesday was chosen for two reasons: the courts, and שקדו, meaning the חכמים wanted the groom to spend Sunday, Monday and Tuesday preparing the feast. Daily courts remove only the first reason. So how can she marry on any day?

keyTerms.meaning: They were careful. The reason that the חכמים cared for women, so the groom prepares the feast for days

phrases.english: But we need 'they were careful'!
phrases.notes: This points to the other reason given earlier: the חכמים made sure the groom would spend three days preparing the feast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that with daily courts a woman may marry any day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second reason, שקדו, is not affected by the courts and still requires Wednesday

steps.title: Where the groom already prepared
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies where the groom already went to the trouble of preparing the feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a case where he already went to the trouble of preparing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'any day' applies when the groom already prepared the feast ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שקדו reason exists only so the feast will be ready. If it is already ready, that reason is also gone. With both reasons gone, she may marry on any day.

keyTerms.meaning: Went to trouble, put in effort

steps.whatToRemember: The Wednesday rule rests on two reasons: courts sitting Thursday, and the groom preparing the feast. Where courts sit daily and the feast is already prepared, a woman may marry on any day.

phrases.english: Where he went to the trouble.
phrases.notes: He means the groom already prepared the feast ahead of time, so he needs no extra days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The feast reason always requires Wednesday
steps.terutzMaskana: When the groom already prepared, the feast reason does not apply
